name: CI

on:
  push:
    # Only the refs that take direct pushes and have no pull request to trigger
    # CI for them. Every other branch reaches CI through the pull_request
    # trigger below; triggering on all pushes made a branch with an open PR run
    # the whole matrix twice for the same commit (verified on sha 2e6afd5d44,
    # which produced both a push run and a pull_request run), doubling demand on
    # the runner pool.
    #
    # release/* is deliberately absent. Release branches are merged through PRs
    # (#7744 head release/2.0.64, #7841 head release/2.0.65), so listing them
    # would preserve exactly the duplication this filter removes: sha 194bd971
    # produced a push run and a pull_request run 9 seconds apart. The PR run on
    # the merge commit is the more relevant gate.
    #
    # Branches pushed without a PR (instrospect, fastjson3, android5/android8,
    # fix/* -- all verified to have zero open PRs) get no CI from this trigger.
    # Validate them by opening a PR or via workflow_dispatch. Note this includes
    # the branch carrying this very change: GitHub evaluates the pushed ref's
    # own workflow file, so this filter cannot be smoke-tested by pushing to the
    # branch that introduces it.
    #
    # `tags` must be listed explicitly: declaring only `branches` excludes tag
    # pushes altogether, and a main-line release tag is the only full-matrix run
    # between merge and publishing to Maven Central. Main-line tag pushes do run
    # this workflow today -- run 30743811143 (head_branch=2.0.64), and 2.0.63 /
    # 2.0.65 likewise. '2.*' covers those and future 2.x releases while
    # excluding the legacy 0.x/1.x tags and the fastcode_*/bak_* scratch tags.
    #
    # Scope of that claim: GitHub evaluates the workflow file at the tagged
    # commit, so this filter only governs tags cut on commits carrying this
    # file. The *.android5 / *.android8 tags are cut on the android5 / android8
    # branches, which still hold a different legacy workflow at this same path
    # (`name: Java CI`, `ubuntu-20.04`, JDK 8/11/17). That runner label is
    # retired, so those runs queue until GitHub's 24-hour cap cancels them --
    # run 33637740678 (tag 2.0.65.android8) went 13:45:57 to 13:46:00 the next
    # day, cancelled. Pre-existing gap, not a regression from this change;
    # porting this file onto android5/android8 is separate work.
    branches:
      - main
      - v2.1.x
    tags:
      - '2.*'
      - 'v2.*'  # the repo already uses a v-prefix for branches (v2.1.x), so a
                # v-prefixed release tag is plausible; missing it fails silently
                # -- no run at all -- on the release gate
    # https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions#example-excluding-paths
    paths-ignore:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '**.md'
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '**.md'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Lane queueing, not compile or test time, dominates CI wall-clock: run
# 34414883838 (29 lanes) spent 94 minutes end to end while its individual lanes
# ran only 3-10 minutes, and its `Test JDK 11 on macos-latest` lane waited 1h26m
# for a runner before running for 8.
#
# That 94 minutes was cross-run contention, and this block does NOT address it.
# The overlapping run was 34330335364 -- a re-run (attempt 2) of a different PR,
# fix-7842-string-to-boolean, whose own 29 lanes spanned 23:00 to 00:31. A group
# keyed per PR cannot suppress another PR's run, nor a main push run. What
# relieves that contention is the 29 -> 15 lane merge below.
#
# This block exists for a narrower and real problem: without it, every new
# commit on the same PR branch queued a fresh full matrix while the previous one
# still held runners, so stale commits on one PR kept saturating the pool.
concurrency:
  # Prefixed because concurrency group names are repository-scoped, not
  # workflow-scoped -- a bare `ci-...` could collide with another workflow here.
  #
  # The group key differs per ref type on purpose:
  #   pull_request -> github.ref (refs/pull/N/merge), stable across commits on
  #                   one PR, so a new commit supersedes the in-flight run.
  #                   This is the block's only real job; it does not deduplicate
  #                   anything on the push side -- the branch/tag filter above
  #                   does that.
  #   push (branch) -> github.sha, unique per commit, so consecutive main
  #                   pushes never share a group and none is dropped. A
  #                   ref-keyed group would let GitHub's default `queue: single`
  #                   silently cancel the pending run when several merges land
  #                   in quick succession. (`queue: max` is documented as
  #                   incompatible with a literal cancel-in-progress: true; this
  #                   file sets it by expression, so that interaction is
  #                   unverified -- sha-keying sidesteps needing `queue` at all.)
  #   push (tag)    -> github.ref (refs/tags/<tag>). A main-line release tag is
  #                   cut on main's HEAD, so the tag push and the main branch
  #                   push carry the SAME sha; sha-keying tags would put the
  #                   release gate in the same group as the main run and queue
  #                   it behind one that has measured at 104 minutes (tag
  #                   2.0.64, sha 39531157: main run 30743786350 at 10:27:40,
  #                   tag run 30743811143 45s later). Tags need neither
  #                   cancellation nor queueing, only a distinct group.
  group: fastjson2-ci-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref_type == 'branch' && github.sha || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write  # Allow posting PR comments for coverage reports

env:
  JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -Duser.timezone=Asia/Shanghai

jobs:
  test:
    # Has to cover the retry path below, not just a healthy run. Measured on run
    # 34414883838: the slowest build-plus-default-suite lane was 10m07s (Test
    # JDK 21 on windows) and the slowest clean-build-plus-reflect-suite lane was
    # 8m22s (Test Reflect JDK 17 on windows). Dropping dokka brings pass 1 to
    # roughly 8m30s, and pass 2 skips the clean and the packaging:
    #   healthy  setup 1 + pass 1 8.5 + pass 2 5    = ~15 min
    #   retry    setup 1 + pass 1 8.5 x2 + pass 2 5 = ~23 min
    # and `cache: maven` adds 2-4 min when it misses cold. 30 covers that; 25
    # did not, and would have died inside pass 2 with an opaque timeout rather
    # than reporting the retry's result.
    #
    # Deliberately not sized to absorb a hang. Every cancelled lane in recent
    # history was the dokka stall documented on the build step below, where the
    # step emitted nothing for ~15 minutes until the cap fired; raising the cap
    # only lets a hang burn more runner time and fail anyway. With dokka gone
    # the remaining stall class is a dependency download, which
    # .mvn/maven.config bounds.
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 16
      matrix:
        java: [ 8, 11, 17, 21, 25 ]
        os: [ ubuntu-24.04, windows-latest, macos-latest ]
        exclude:
          # Exclude JDK 25 on macOS (not yet supported)
          - java: 25
            os: macos-latest
    name: Test JDK ${{ matrix.java }} on ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Cache Maven wrapper distribution
        # `setup-java`'s `cache: maven` only caches ~/.m2/repository. The wrapper
        # downloads apache-maven-*-bin.zip into ~/.m2/wrapper on first use, which
        # is the step that failed on windows-latest (run 33629858155).
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.m2/wrapper
          key: maven-wrapper-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties') }}
          restore-keys: |
            maven-wrapper-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: zulu
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      - name: Build with Maven and test (default creator)
        # This job absorbed the former test-reflect job, which repeated the
        # entire reactor build and differed only by -Dfastjson2.creator=reflect
        # at test time. Running the suite twice over one build halves the lane
        # count (28 -> 14), which is what relieves the runner queue.
        #
        # -Pgen-dokka is deliberately not passed. dokka resolves its ~99 MB
        # runtime tree at mojo execution time and is the sole source of every
        # cancelled lane in recent history -- 7 confirmed, all ubuntu, all
        # default-creator, all with one signature: job 111846711588 printed the
        # dokka banner at 15:52:16, then emitted nothing at all until the
        # 20-minute cap killed it at 16:07:12, leaving an orphaned java process.
        # They include job 90506607532, which cancelled the 2.0.63 release-tag
        # gate with 28 of 29 lanes green, and job 112155369041, dated after
        # #7883 merged -- so the aether timeouts in .mvn/maven.config do not
        # bound it. Dokka output is JDK- and OS-independent, so 14 lanes
        # validated nothing one lane wouldn't.
        #
        # The profile still activates on performRelease=true
        # (kotlin/pom.xml:96-101), so release builds keep generating it and the
        # published artifacts are unchanged. The trade is where a dokka break
        # surfaces: kotlin is 12th of 17 in the reactor and deploy-settings
        # binds nexus-staging:deploy per module, so a release-time dokka failure
        # strands the ~11 modules already uploaded to staging and needs a manual
        # drop. It cannot publish a broken artifact -- close is never reached,
        # and Central requires the kotlin javadoc jar that only dokka produces.
        #
        # -Pgen-javadoc stays: doclint behaviour is JDK-dependent and it has
        # never hung. Javadoc is hermetic now: the gen-javadoc profile disables
        # detectJavaApiLink and codegen no longer declares a docs.oracle.com
        # <link>, so no lane resolves external URLs. Before that, a transient
        # runner DNS fault hard-failed the 2.0.64 tag gate.
        #
        # shell: bash is required, not cosmetic. windows-latest defaults to
        # pwsh -- confirmed from a windows test lane's job log, which records
        # `shell: C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.EXE -command ". '{0}'"`.
        # The retry below is written in bash: `|| { ... }` and the
        # `MVNW_REPOURL=... ./mvnw` environment prefix are not pwsh syntax, so
        # the mirror fallback cannot behave as intended there. Until now all 5
        # windows test lanes ran this block under pwsh, while the windows
        # test-reflect lanes -- which did declare bash -- were the ones that
        # actually depended on the fallback.
        shell: bash
        # Retry once on failure: a stalled dependency download now fails fast
        # (see .mvn/maven.config) and the retry resumes from the partially
        # populated ~/.m2. MVNW_REPOURL lets the Maven wrapper itself fall back
        # to the GCS Maven Central mirror when repo.maven.apache.org is
        # unreachable from the runner (observed on windows-latest).
        run: |
          ./mvnw -V --no-transfer-progress -Pgen-javadoc clean package || {
            echo "::warning::Maven build failed; retrying once with the GCS Maven Central mirror as fallback"
            sleep 10
            MVNW_REPOURL=https://maven-central.storage-download.googleapis.com/maven2 ./mvnw -V --no-transfer-progress -Pgen-javadoc clean package
          }

      - name: Test again with -Dfastjson2.creator=reflect
        # Kept as its own step so a red lane still says which suite failed --
        # the job name no longer carries "Reflect" -- and so each pass's
        # duration stays visible in the job summary.
        #
        # No `clean`: this reuses the classes the previous step compiled. It has
        # to be the `test` phase, not a bare `surefire:test` goal. A bare goal
        # never runs `package` for the sibling modules, so Maven's ReactorReader
        # has no artifact to serve for them and resolution dies with "Could not
        # find artifact com.alibaba.fastjson2:fastjson2:jar:...-SNAPSHOT" even
        # though the jar is sitting in core/target/ from the previous step.
        #
        # No retry, which is a deliberate change: the former test-reflect job
        # retried its whole `clean package` on any failure, flaky tests
        # included. This pass downloads nothing new -- the previous step already
        # resolved every dependency, and this one stops at the `test` phase so it
        # never reaches the javadoc-jar binding at `package` -- so a failure here
        # is a test failure, and re-running would only delay reporting it.
        shell: bash
        run: ./mvnw -V --no-transfer-progress -Dfastjson2.creator=reflect test

  coverage:
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0  # Fetch all history for better coverage analysis

      - name: Cache Maven wrapper distribution
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.m2/wrapper
          key: maven-wrapper-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties') }}
          restore-keys: |
            maven-wrapper-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Set up JDK 11
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: zulu
          java-version: 11
          cache: maven

      - name: Build with Maven and generate coverage
        # Same transient-download retry as the test job.
        run: |
          ./mvnw -V --no-transfer-progress clean package || {
            echo "::warning::Maven build failed; retrying once with the GCS Maven Central mirror as fallback"
            sleep 10
            MVNW_REPOURL=https://maven-central.storage-download.googleapis.com/maven2 ./mvnw -V --no-transfer-progress clean package
          }
        env:
          CI: true  # Explicitly set CI to ensure JaCoCo profile is activated

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        # v5 runs natively on the Node.js 24 runtime; v4 targets Node 20, which
        # runners now force onto Node 24, where the upload intermittently dies
        # with EPROTO SSL handshake errors that fail the step despite
        # fail_ci_if_error: false.
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          name: codecov-umbrella
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          flags: unittests
          fail_ci_if_error: false
          verbose: true

### 启动方式

运行 SolonTestApp.main 方法（或者直接运行单测 DemoTest ）

###  测试

测试 Render 是否正常工作

* 访问：[http://localhost:8080/demo?username=world&password=1234](http://localhost:8080/demo?username=world&password=1234)

测试 找不到的地址异常（技术上和上面一样，Solon 所有的 Web 输出都会走：Render 接口）

* 访问：[http://localhost:8080/error](http://localhost:8080/error)

### 说明

此演示，会自动触发 fastjson2-extension-solon 的:

* Fastjson2RenderFactory 
* Fastjson2ActionExecutor
